Report Description/// UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1381234 /// THE RP CONFIRMED 1875 LITRES OF DIESEL SPILLED TO GROUND THROUGH A CORRODED PLUG AT THE BOTTOM OF THE TANK. A QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL (QP), ACTIVE EARTH ENGINEERING LTD., HAS PROVIDED AN INITIAL RESPONSE ASSESSMENT AND RECOMMENDATIONS. HARD AND SOFT FIXED BOOM REMAINS IN PLACE IN THE BAY AND CONTINUES TO BE EFFECTIVE CONTAINING ANY RECOVERABLE PRODUCT ON THE WATER. BOOM WILL REMAIN IN PLACE UNTIL MONITORING SHOWS NO ADDITIONAL CONTAMINATION. THE RP WILL CONTINUE TO USE ABSORBENT PADS, PARTICULARLY AT THE BASE OF THE ROCK EMBANKMENT UNTIL THE DIESEL STOPS SEEPING OUT IN THE AREA. THE QP BIOLOGIST HAS STATED THE AREA WILL RECOVER OVER TIME DUE TO PRODUCT EVAPORATION, ULTRAVIOLET DEGRADATION OF THE DIESEL, AND WAVE ACTION. RP WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR SOILS AND CHANGES TO VEGETATION AND WILDLIFE HEALTH WILL BE NOTED UNTIL THE AREA HAS RETURNED TO PREDISTURBANCE CONDITIONS. AS SPILL SITE CONDITIONS CONTINUE TO IMPROVE, CURRENT RESPONSE EFFORTS ARE EXPECTED TO TRANSITION TO RECOVERY FOR LONG-TERM MONITORING AND REMEDIATION EFFORTS. THE INCIDENT IS BEING DOWNGRADED TO CODE 1 NOTIFICATIONS, WITH NO FURTHER UPDATES EXPECTED. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION: NEEC REPORT THE CALLER DISCOVERED THE DIESEL TANK HAD BEEN INTEREFERED WITH AND 3/4 OF THE TANK HAS BEEN PUMPED INTO THE TRINCOMALI CANAL.
